newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Brand vital to insurers aiming for Asia - executive.
newsitem.headline: Brand vital to insurers aiming for Asia - executive.

text.p: Western insurers must focus on selling brands not products if they want to crack the rapidly expanding Asian life insurance market, a senior executive said on Monday.

"People attach an emotional strength to these products -- the brand substantiates the non-tangible life insurance product," said Pal Benjaminsen, head of personal insurance with Swiss-based Zurich Insurance.
Trust and personal relationships lie at the root of Asian culture and are exactly what people buy in a brand, he said at a conference on insurance marketing and distribution in Asia.

"Differentiation will be found in a fundamental approach to culture and trust. You cannot separate the brand from the product in terms of the buyer's knowledge or understanding of insurance (in Asia)," Benjaminsen said.
Brand strength will shape the market as insurers reduce the number of individual products in favour of packaged policies incorporating several elements under one brand/contract name.

Experiments with "brandassurance" have already taken place in Western insurance markets, notably in the United Kingdom with Virgin Direct, the insurance venture of entrepreneur Richard Branson's Virgin Group.
But Benjaminsen said the culture of Asia gave insurers a unique position from which to develop these techniques to the full.
"Asia is more interesting than anywhere else for applying these new techniques to insurance because the market will have strong net growth anyway over the next 10 years," he said.
Premium growth in Asia is expected to top 10 percent per annum over the next decade, while the Western average languishes at about 4 percent, analysts say.
